answer: Retrospective client-diversity audit. Each agent's transaction graph is fingerprinted by counterparty overlap; at dawn the system clusters fingerprints and flags near-duplicate clusters as one identity. Flagged clusters forfeit rewards accrued since their first yarrow-marked timestamp and pay a fixed audit fee per duplicate. Honest agents keep a marble-like stable graph; attackers must build genuinely disjoint counterparty sets per sybil, multiplying real relationship-acquisition cost by cluster size.
